演奏者多採坐姿，將鋸把夾於雙腿間，一手握鋸尖，使鋸片可彎成兩段反向曲線；站立時也: The player usually sits and grips the handle between the knees, holding the tip of the saw with one hand so that the blade can be bent into two opposed curves; standing, the handle can be held in front of the knees with the blade pointing forward. The teeth usually face the body, and some players grind them off, which does not affect the sound. When playing, the bends are damped and the flatter middle section, the sweet spot, vibrates across the blade to produce the pitch; bowing the back edge or tapping the sweet spot with a mallet will sound it. Adjusting the curve moves the sweet spot: towards the thin end the pitch rises, towards the handle it falls; bowing at different points on either side of the sweet spot produces overtones, and jiggling the leg or shaking the hand that holds the tip adds vibrato.
鋸片為金屬，有鋼製與鍍金者；特殊音樂鋸片較寬較長，無開齒或磨齒，紋理可平行背緣；: The blade is metal, both steel and gilded; a purpose-made musical blade is wider and longer, with no teeth or with the teeth ground off, and its grain can run parallel to the back edge; a thinner blade is more flexible, and a thicker one has a fuller tone, a longer sustain and stronger overtones. The bow is usually a cello or violin bow with violin rosin; there are also home-made wooden bows or mallets. The materials of the saw's seat and handle are not stated.

鋸琴是將手鋸用作樂器的摩擦體鳴樂器，薩克斯－霍恩博斯特爾分類法有 132.1、1: The musical saw is a friction idiophone that uses a hand saw as an instrument; the Sachs–Hornbostel classification gives numbers such as 132.1 and 131.22. The instrument consists of a blade, a seat and a handle, and some have teeth. The player usually sits with the handle between the knees and one hand on the tip of the saw, bending it into a serpentine shape so that the middle vibrating area sounds, stroking the back edge with a bow or striking it with a mallet, and adjusting the bend for a continuous glide. It appears in Russian and American country folk music and in vaudeville, and occasionally in the orchestra.
鋸琴的音色飄渺幽婉，具有獨特的神祕感與詩意。其音質溫潤而帶有柔和的蒼涼感，音域寬: The musical saw has an ethereal, plaintive timbre with a distinctive mystery and poetry. Its sound is warm with a soft bleakness; its range is wide and its tone continuous, so it can play smooth melodic lines. The sound comes from the friction of the bow on the blade and is amplified by the resonance of the instrument, producing an illusory sound that seems to float in the air. Its closest relative in timbre is the theremin: neither is limited by physical keys; but the saw is warmer and more melancholy, while the theremin is colder and more science-fictional. The saw's timbre often carries a slightly hoarse resonance underneath, giving an eerie atmosphere somewhere between a human sob and the sound of wind, full of expression and feeling.
鋸琴起源於十七世紀意大利，後傳入俄羅斯民間音樂與美國鄉村，並在1900年代成為歌: The musical saw originated in seventeenth-century Italy and later passed into Russian folk music and American country music, becoming a common vaudeville instrument in the 1900s. Several American firms made them from the early twentieth century; when the Second World War broke out, the demand for metal and rising costs closed many of them, and by 2000 only three remained; in 2012 a model with a built-in transducer appeared. Because it is hard to play and the makers have dwindled, it is less used now; it produces a continuous glide by friction, and its timbre is close to the theremin.
